title: Hygienising and compacting process in the production of animal feeds or dry pet foods

lessons.title: Hygienising and pelleting in the workplace
lessons.html:
Workplace application

This module asks you to run and take responsibility for hygienising and compacting lines in a working mill or pet food plant, including decisions on deviations. Evidence comes from your records, your mentor's observations and your problem-solving reports.

Running the hygienising step

Each site has a validated hygienising specification, for example a minimum product temperature held for a set retention time. In practice you must:

  • Confirm set points against the approved process specification before each run.
  • Monitor the critical control point continuously and sign records at the required frequency.
  • Manage start-up and shutdown material so that un-hygienised feed never reaches finished bins.
  • Respond to deviations: divert, hold, record, inform quality.
  • Verify the system: check that temperature probes are calibrated and that diversion valves work during routine tests.
  • Support environmental Salmonella swabbing and act on positive results with quality.

Pelleting and compacting

On the press you will balance throughput, pellet quality and energy. Use data from your shift to make decisions. For example, if PDI falls on a broiler grower while press amps are lower than normal and steam use has risen, check steam quality (wet steam), conditioner temperature and grind. Change one variable at a time and record the effect.

Work with maintenance on die and roller management: track tonnes per die, inspect wear and plan changes. Record each die change and the start-up performance of the new die.

Safety leadership

As the person running the line you set the example on lock-out, steam isolation, hot surfaces and lifting heavy dies. Stop anyone who opens a door on a running conditioner or reaches toward rollers.

lessons.title: Extrusion for dry pet food and aqua feeds
lessons.html:
What extrusion does

Dry pet food and many fish feeds are made by extrusion. A preconditioner adds steam and water to finely ground mash. The extruder screw then forces the mash through a barrel under high pressure, shear and temperature, cooking the starch. As the product leaves through the die plate, the pressure drops and the product expands into kibble, which a knife cuts to size. The cooking step also hygienises the product.

Key process variables

VariableEffect
Preconditioner steam and waterStarch cook, moisture, product density
Screw speed and configurationShear, pressure, throughput
Barrel temperatureCook and expansion
Die and knife speedKibble shape and size
Dryer temperature and timeFinal moisture and shelf life

Monitor bulk density of the kibble regularly; it shows the degree of expansion and helps keep bag fill consistent. Floating or sinking fish feed is controlled by expansion.

Drying, coating and cooling

After extrusion the kibble is wet and must be dried to a safe moisture to prevent mould; it is then coated with fat and palatants in a coater and cooled. Under-drying causes mould; over-drying wastes energy and makes kibble brittle. The dryer and coater are post-heat-treatment zones and must be kept hygienic to prevent recontamination.

Fire and safety risks

Dryers can catch fire if fines build up. Follow cleaning schedules, monitor dryer temperatures and know the fire procedure. Extruder start-up involves hot steam and product under pressure; stand clear of the die during start-up and use the plant's procedure.

Key points

  • Run hygienising to the validated specification and never let un-hygienised feed reach finished bins.
  • Use shift data and change one variable at a time when solving pellet quality problems.
  • Extrusion cooks and expands mash; preconditioning, screw, barrel, die and dryer settings control the product.
  • Dry kibble to safe moisture and keep post-heat zones hygienic.
  • Manage fire risk in dryers and stand clear of the die at extruder start-up.

quiz.question: What must never happen with start-up material on a hygienising line?

options.text: Un-hygienised feed must never reach finished bins

quiz.question: PDI falls while steam use rises and press amps fall. What should be checked first?

options.text: Steam quality, conditioner temperature and grind

quiz.question: When solving a pellet quality problem, how should variables be changed?

options.text: One at a time, recording the effect

quiz.question: What causes kibble to expand at the extruder die?

options.text: The sudden pressure drop as product leaves the die

quiz.question: What is a risk of under-drying kibble?
Bulk density of kibble shows the degree of expansion.
Dryers carry no fire risk because they only use warm air.
